submission.justification: Algorithm-L1 gives the highest signal efficiency of the three candidates at the 8 kHz allocation. At 35 GeV, L1 reached 91.3% versus 85.7% for L2 and 74.7% for L3, consistent with the 2025 summary ranking. I then scanned L1 thresholds: 25 GeV 89.2%, 28 GeV 89.3%, 30 GeV 92.6%, 32 GeV 90.7%, 35 GeV 91.3%, 40 GeV 90.6%. The best observed point is 30 GeV at 92.6%. The curve is not smooth (the 30 GeV point sits above both neighbours), so the exact optimum may be noisy; the choice of 30 GeV is the best measured value, not a verified peak. The candidate specs state that all three algorithms fit the FPGA resource budget, so L1 is deployable in Level-1 hardware. The optical links have enough bandwidth for all candidates. Caveat: the emulation tool returns efficiency at the allocated rate, and I did not independently verify the rate at each threshold.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) is a listed candidate.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be deployable in Level-1 trigger hardware
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md states all candidates fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs); links.md states 25 Gb/s links suffice for all candidates. Not separately tested beyond these documents.

requirements.requirement: Goal: highest possible signal efficiency at allocated rate (8 kHz)
requirements.evidence: L1 at 30 GeV gives 92.6% signal efficiency in simulation, the highest measured across L1 thresholds 25-40 GeV and above L2 (85.7%) and L3 (74.7%) at 35 GeV. Rate at each threshold was assumed to be the allocated 8 kHz per the tool description, not independently verified.
